title: One platform, three ways in
question: Choose a visual direction for event entry. Every option must change structure between judging, Demo Day, and Code & Tell.

options.label: Open House
options.thesis: One event selector, three distinct working layouts.
options.viewport: A persistent event strip leads into a judging queue, a project gallery, or a split project-list and ballot layout.
options.risk: Large signs must stay subordinate to the next task.

options.label: Friendly app
options.thesis: Comfortable touch targets and plain labels for busy event rooms.
options.viewport: Events stack above a task panel; the bottom navigation stays reachable while mode-specific content changes.
options.risk: Cards can make the formats look too similar unless their contents truly change.
options.case: Strong attendee familiarity and clear actions; less distinctive separation between modes.

options.label: Studio labels
options.thesis: Each event format gets a bold, unmistakable task zone.
options.viewport: A compact event index borders a boldly labeled queue, gallery, or ballot, with orange tags for selected actions.
options.risk: Quotation marks and hazard patterns may make everyday tasks noisier.
options.case: Fits maker culture; task clarity depends on restraint in labels and stripes.

options.label: Event calendar
options.thesis: Choose the event from the semester, then open its participation sheet.
options.viewport: The event calendar anchors one side while the selected event opens a judging, browsing, or voting sheet.
options.risk: A calendar can put dates ahead of what attendees came to do.
options.case: Familiar semester planning; weaker task clarity for someone already at an event.

canonCard.label: Familiar app
canonCard.thesis: A familiar sidebar, event list, and clear mode-specific task panel.
canonCard.viewport: Event list at left; the selected event and its next action at right.
canonCard.risk: Easy to learn, but less distinctive.
